name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: Cheap large drugmaker with steady cash flow and new drugs coming in to offset Keytruda's patent expiry; it steadies the portfolio.
targets.risks: Revenue gap when Keytruda loses patent protection, and US drug-price pressure.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: Pipeline and gas-processing company paid mostly by volume, with Permian volumes growing and payouts to shareholders rising.
targets.risks: Permian drilling slows if oil prices fall.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: Leading US steelmaker with a strong balance sheet, helped by import tariffs and infrastructure and data-center construction demand.
targets.risks: Steel prices fall if demand softens.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: Leader in cybersecurity software, with recurring revenue speeding up and customers using more of its modules.
targets.risks: High valuation leaves little room for any disappointment.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: Refiner returning a lot of cash to shareholders, with refinery use high and a stake in the MPLX pipeline business supporting results.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: Specialty-materials company after its breakup, with better profit margins and electronics exposure that may be undervalued.
targets.risks: Industrial demand weakens or the breakup is poorly executed.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: Very cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt and buying back shares.
targets.risks: Generic price erosion and manufacturing-quality problems.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: Efficient refiner that just had a strong quarter; the 10% drop looks like profit-taking, not a broken thesis.
targets.risks: Profit margins fall and refined-product inventories rise.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: Data-storage company at a reasonable valuation, helped by demand for all-flash storage and AI data storage.
targets.risks: Companies cut tech spending and the shift to cloud continues.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Results got better (billings +29%, guidance raised) while the stock fell, so the valuation reset makes holding reasonable.
targets.risks: The firewall upgrade wave peaks and growth slows into 2027.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: Maker of electronic test equipment, positioned for a recovery in AI and data-center, semiconductor and communications spending.
targets.risks: Orders recover more slowly than expected.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth-management and investment-banking firm, helped by a pickup in deals and strong market activity; financials are leading the market.
targets.risks: Market downturn hits trading and advisory fees.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Leader in gene sequencing at a low valuation, with a margin recovery and possible new product launches as catalysts.
targets.risks: China restrictions and weak research-lab budgets.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
